cues.text: Erm … hello Professor, I’m John Wishart. I’m working on my entry for the Global Design Competition. My tutor said you might be able to help me with it.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: Ah, yes, I got a copy of your drawings. Come in and tell me about it. What sort of competition is it?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Well, it’s an international design competition and we have to come up with a new design for a typical domestic kitchen appliance.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: I see, and are there any special conditions? Does it have to save energy for example?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Actually that was the focus in last year’s competition. This year’s different. We have to adopt an innovative approach to existing technology, using it in a way that hasn’t been thought of before.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: I see, that sounds tricky. And what kitchen appliance have you chosen?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: I decided to choose a dishwasher.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: Interesting. What makes you choose that?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Well, they’re an everyday kitchen appliance in most Australian houses but they’re all pretty boring and almost identical to each other. I think some people will be prepared to pay a little extra for something that looks different.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: That’s a nice idea. I see you’ve called your design ‘the Rockpool’; why is that?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Basically because it looks like the rock pools you find on a beach. The top is made of glass so that you can look down into it.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: And there’s a stone at the bottom. Is that just for decoration?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Actually it does have a function. Instead of pushing a button, you turn the stone.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: So it’s really just a novel way of starting the dishwasher.
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: That’s right.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: It’s a really nice design, but what makes it innovative?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Well, I decided to make a dishwasher that uses carbon dioxide.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: In place of water and detergent? How will you manage that?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: The idea is to pressurize the carbon dioxide so that it becomes a liquid. The fluid is then released into the dishwasher where it cleans the dishes all by itself.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: Sounds like a brilliant idea! Your system will totally do away with the need for strong detergents. So what happens once the dishes are clean?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Well, to allow them to dry, the liquid carbon dioxide and the waste materials all go to an area called the holding chamber. That’s where the liquid is depressurised and so it reverts to a gas. Then the oil and grease are separated out and sent to the waste system.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: It sounds like you’ve thought it all out very thoroughly. So, what happens to the carbon dioxide once the process is complete? Not wasted I hope.
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Actually, that’s where the real savings are made. The carbon dioxide is sent back to the cylinder and can be used again and again.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: What a terrific idea. Do you think it will ever be built?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Probably not, but that’s OK.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: Well, I’m sure a lot of positive things will come out of your design.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: Now, you seem to have thought about everything so what exactly did you need me to help you with?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Well, my design has made it to the final stage of the competition and, in a few months’ time. I have to give a presentation, and that’s the part I was hoping you could help me with.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: Right, well that should be easy enough. What have you managed to do so far?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Well, I’ve got detailed drawings to show how it will work and I’ve also written a 500-word paper on it.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: I see. Well, if you want to stand a good chance of winning you really need a model of the machine.
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Yes, I thought I might but I’m having a few problems.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: What is the main difficulty so far? Let me guess – is it the materials?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Yes. I want it to look professional but everything that’s top quality is also very expensive.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: Look, projects like this are very important to us. They really help lift our profile. So why don’t you talk to the university about a grant? I can help you fill out the application forms if you like.
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: That would be a great.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: You’d better show me this paper you’ve written as well. For a global competition such as this you need to make sure the technical details you’ve given are accurate and thorough.
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: That would be a great help.
cues.speaker: JOHN

cues.text: Is there anything else I can do?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Well, I’m really …
cues.speaker: JOHN
